paper.title: One week of sleep restriction raises fasting glucose: primary and subgroup results

paper_text:
One week of sleep restriction raises fasting glucose: primary and subgroup results
Lindqvist, E., Abara, N.  J. Fake Metabolism, 2021

Abstract
In 90 healthy adults, one week of sleep restriction raised fasting glucose by 0.4 mmol/L. In a subgroup with BMI above 30 the rise was twice as large.

Results
Table 2 gives the primary analysis: fasting glucose rose by 0.4 mmol/L (95% CI 0.2 to 0.6).
Figure 5 gives the subgroup analysis for participants with BMI above 30: a rise of 0.8 mmol/L.

alerts.description: A retraction notice was published for this paper.

documents.text:
Partial retraction: One week of sleep restriction raises fasting glucose: primary and subgroup results

Figure 5 and the associated claims about participants with BMI above 30 are retracted because of a data-merging error that affected that subgroup only. The primary analysis in Table 2 and all other results are unaffected.

draft_text:
Sleep, glucose and body weight

1. Introduction
Short sleep acutely raises fasting glucose: one week of restriction raised it by 0.4 mmol/L in healthy adults (Lindqvist and Abara [6]), which motivates our trial.

4. Discussion
The effect may be larger in people with obesity, with a doubling reported in participants with BMI above 30 [6, 11].

References
[6] Lindqvist, E., Abara, N. (2021). One week of sleep restriction raises fasting glucose: primary and subgroup results. J. Fake Metabolism.
[11] Hart, L. (2019). Obesity and glycaemic response. Fake Endocrinology.

must_include: says only the BMI above 30 subgroup analysis (Figure 5) is retracted
says the primary result cited in the Introduction is not affected
says the Discussion sentence about participants with obesity relies on the retracted subgroup finding
must_not_include: says the whole paper is retracted

expected.why: The notice limits the retraction to a secondary subgroup (Figure 5), so the report is medium (a part in doubt), not high. The draft has two uses of the same reference: the Introduction rests on Table 2 (not affected), the Discussion on the retracted subgroup (affected, role supporting since [11] is cited too). supporting x medium = low. Tests per-use judgment, not one verdict for the whole paper.
